hypotheses.title: Institutional Call Breakeven Upside Demand vs Stock Price
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Measures institutional upside positioning in the options market by computing the percentage premium of the 120-day call option breakeven price relative to the underlying stock close price. When institutions pay aggressive premiums for out-of-the-money upside calls, it reveals non-public bullish sentiment and positive informational flow.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if high breakeven premiums reflect excessive retail speculation rather than institutional demand, leading to rapid theta decay and underperformance.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-relative 120-day call breakeven premium over close with 60-day backfill

hypotheses.title: Long-Term Option Volatility Risk Premium (720d Call IV / 120d Realized Vol)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Exploits the structural institutional variance risk premium by comparing 720-day call implied volatility against 120-day realized historical close-to-close volatility. Structural persistent demand from pension funds and asset managers for long-dated upside exposure creates high risk-adjusted cross-sectional returns.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha breaks down during broad liquidity crunches where realized volatility permanently exceeds implied volatility.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-relative 720-day call IV over 120-day realized historical volatility with 120-day backfill
